svg.title: ABYSSAL architecture (portrait)
svg.desc: Read from the bottom up. Inputs (documents, tracks, recordings, public layers, sketches) get receipts and an origin tag. Measurements go through fifteen signal engines that share one contract: physics forward model, inference, calibration, contact. Contacts pass an admission gate (calibrated, then admitted by a person) into the evidence-to-belief engine: observations, likelihood, provenance pooling, negative evidence, add and normalise. Claims enter that engine directly. The posterior feeds where next and Plan Studio, the Search Ledger, influence in bits and the audit trail, which produce the next search, the belief map, the Evidence Map and the dossier.

g.data-desc: Ranks candidate searches by expected information gain, splits effort across assets (water-filling under exponential detection), prices it, and draws the search-to-exhaustion curve with its stopping point.
g.title: Plan Studio

g.data-desc: Which area to search next, with which asset, what it is worth and the point at which searching stops paying.
g.title: Next search
g.text: where, with what, and what it

g.data-desc: Where the probability has gone: still unsearched, searched and missed, or outside the drawn area; plus Search Health checks for seven named traps.
g.title: Search Ledger

g.data-desc: The probability map of where the object is, with credible regions. Only admitted observations ever change it.
g.title: Belief map

g.data-desc: The Kullback–Leibler divergence between the map with and without each item, and each whole source, so you can see what is carrying the answer.
g.title: Influence, in bits
g.text: KL divergence per item and per

g.data-desc: How far each item and each whole source moved the map, in bits, with exact undo.
g.title: Evidence Map
g.text: what moved the belief, and how

g.data-desc: Every result records the model version, code commit and input hashes, and every admission records who made it and when.
g.title: Audit trail

g.data-desc: An exportable record of the case: every source with its receipt, every computation with its model version, code commit and input hashes.
g.title: Dossier
g.text: an audit pack anyone can re-run

g.data-desc: The only way into the belief map. A detector's output is a contact; only a calibrated detector (measured detection and false-alarm rates) can propose an observation, and a person must admit it. Agents propose, code acquires, humans admit. Automatic fusion of engine output into belief is deliberately parked.
g.title: Admission gate

g.data-desc: What every engine returns: a position (or time, depth, identity), its uncertainty, a score, and what is needed to reproduce it. A contact is never evidence by itself.
g.title: Contact

g.data-desc: Every engine is scored on SCENARIO data with a known answer: how often it finds the target, how often it raises false alarms, and whether its intervals contain the truth as often as they claim. The radar engines can also self-calibrate on REAL data from ships that broadcast AIS.
g.title: Calibration

g.data-desc: Turns measurements into an estimate: matched filters and constant-false-alarm detectors, multi-target tracking with optimal assignment, Levenberg–Marquardt fits, stationary-phase chirps, cepstra, likelihood grids with analytic marginalisation.
g.title: Inference

g.data-desc: Each engine starts from the physics: Kelvin wakes and azimuth shift, dispersion of impact waves, sound in the SOFAR channel, a magnetic dipole in Earth's field, leeway drift, bubble oscillation, radar backscatter from a wind-roughened sea.
g.title: Physics forward model
g.text: what the data would be if the

a.data-desc: Finds ships in radar images (CFAR), reads their wakes for heading and speed, and matches them to AIS; ships with no AIS are dark.
a.title: SAR vessels & wakes

a.data-desc: Links dark detections across satellite passes with Kalman filters and optimal assignment; flags loitering, rendezvous and possible identities.
a.title: Dark tracks

a.data-desc: Every AIS ship the radar should have seen is a free labelled trial: detection rate by length and wind, on your own sensor.
a.title: AIS self-calibration

a.data-desc: Reads sea-surface wind from the radar backscatter (CMOD5.n) and wind streaks, because wind decides what a miss means.
a.title: Wind from radar

a.data-desc: Stacks many passes: what is always there (platforms, buoys), what keeps coming back (anchorages), what passes through.
a.title: Persistence

a.data-desc: Ranks vessels whose AIS went silent before a pass against each dark contact: reach, dead reckoning, length.
a.title: Who went dark?

a.data-desc: The splash clock: an impact's ring waves disperse, so one image gives the centre and the time since impact.
a.title: Impact rings

a.data-desc: Matched-filter bank for debris rings, crater rims and slick rings at many radii.
a.title: Ring finder

a.data-desc: Locates a bang from arrival-time differences at a few hydrophones, with a correlated error model and a mispick alarm.
a.title: Hydrophone TDOA

a.data-desc: Locates an event across an ocean basin from distant hydrophones; land blocks paths, and silence on open water is evidence.
a.title: SOFAR basin

a.data-desc: Reads the bubble-pulse period of an implosion or explosion: size against depth, and depth when the hull volume is known.
a.title: Implosion forensics

a.data-desc: Fits a magnetic dipole to a survey in Earth's field: position, depth and moment, induced or remanent.
a.title: Magnetic dipole

a.data-desc: Finds compact relief in multibeam (including NOAA BlueTopo) and highlight–shadow pairs in side-scan.
a.title: Seabed & sonar

a.data-desc: Runs recovered debris backwards through wind and current to where it entered the water, sharing the uncertain environment.
a.title: Debris back-track

a.data-desc: On land: finds small objects whose colour does not belong (a tent, a tarp, a vehicle) in Sentinel-2 imagery, with the RX detector.
a.title: Spectral anomalies

a.data-desc: Engines chain: a hydrophone fix (SOFAR), a collapse depth from the bubble pulse with the hull volume, and the seabed together rule out water too shallow for the implosion.
a.title: Lost-submarine drill

g.data-desc: The posterior is a sum in log space: the prior (terrain, drift, leeway or walking motion) plus every admitted likelihood, then normalised. Probability outside the drawn area is kept explicitly, never silently renormalised away. Six versioned models, each selectable.
g.title: Add & normalise
g.text: log prior + Σ log L; outside-

g.data-desc: A search that found nothing still moves the map: each searched cell is multiplied by the chance of missing, 1 − POD, a sum of log(1 − POD) in log space.
g.title: Negative evidence

g.data-desc: Five reports that all trace back to one witness are one piece of evidence, not five. Items that share a provenance root are pooled before they enter the map.
g.title: Provenance pooling
g.text: echoes of one root count once

g.data-desc: Each observation becomes a likelihood over the grid, weighted by its reliability and grouped by family so correlated evidence is not double counted.
g.title: Likelihood

g.data-desc: Explicit, reviewable claims: a point with uncertainty, a bearing, a range ring, a corridor, a 'not here' area statement, a completed search with its POD.
g.title: Observations

g.data-desc: Everything in the Ops console and most map layers is context: it helps a person see and reason, but it cannot change the belief map. To count, it must become an explicit observation and be admitted.
g.title: Context, never evidence

g.data-desc: Every item carries its origin: REAL or SCENARIO. Synthetic data is tagged end to end and can never enter a real case, so simulators and answer keys live safely alongside real evidence.
g.title: Origin tag
g.text: REAL or SCENARIO on every item

g.data-desc: Every acquired file and fetched window gets a receipt, and every item records the root it descends from. Results record model version, code commit and input hashes, so anything can be reproduced and defended later.
g.title: Receipts & provenance
g.text: URL · time · SHA-256 · licence · provenance root

g.data-desc: Witness statements, logs, reports and papers. Read by a person or proposed by an agent; a person decides what each one claims.
g.title: Docs

g.data-desc: Vessel and aircraft tracks: AIS archives (including NOAA MarineCadastre day files), ADS-B, GPS logs. Context until a fix is used as evidence.
g.title: Tracks

g.data-desc: Raw measurements for the signal engines: radar images, acoustic recordings, magnetometer surveys, multibeam and side-scan.
g.title: Sensors

g.data-desc: Opt-in public datasets fetched with receipts: depth, relief, magnetics, gravity, satellite radar and imagery.
g.title: Layers

g.data-desc: What an analyst draws or types: a sighting, a bearing, a corridor, a 'not here' statement, a completed search.
g.title: Sketches
